references.text: God's original instruction to Moses to make the curtain for the entrance of the tent with blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, embroidered work. Exodus 36:37 describes the execution of this command.
Describes the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, also made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen with embroidered work, showing the parallel in the tabernacle's textiles.
Refers to the craftsmen who were filled with wisdom to perform embroidery work in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen—the same materials and techniques used in 36:37.
Describes the curtain for the gate of the courtyard with the same materials: blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, embroidered work.
The priests' sash was also made of fine twisted linen, blue, purple, and scarlet with embroidered work, showing the consistent use of these materials in the sanctuary.
The same instruction given in chapter 26, carried out exactly as written in chapter 36.
The temple entrance is the permanent fulfillment of the tabernacle's design, with identical symbolism.
Complementary verse: The instruction for the inner dividing curtain is compared with the outer entrance area.
